Elliott, of the T.C.C., made up ground on Bowers and a bad take-over between the latter and Hayes saw Holmes send off the T.C.C. man in the lead for the final quarter.

This brought us to the 1 Mile Medley Relay, and the South team was:— Herbert, Bowers, Hayes, Marchant, which made the third time of running for Marchant and Bowers, and the second for the other two, which speaks volumes for their pluck and sportsmanship.
4 x 200 Yards (Shuttle).—1, Police; 2, Belgrave (Hayes, Harding, Metcalfe and Wright).—43.4. 4 x 220 Relay.—1, Police; 2, Belgrave (Hayes, Harding, Metcalfe and Wright).—1. 35.6.

Norton, who has recently joined the Club, won the 100 Yards in good style, with George Hayes finishing third. In the 880 Yards the Whitgift boys were too good for our Juniors, of whom however, Brown ran very promisingly.
The 100 Yards, won in 10.1s., saw Peter Vine about a yard away with Hayes fourth. Peter stepped into the breach and tackled the quarter, and was a good third in 54.1.
(Morris, Clay, Hayes, Bishop). 4.8½ Scoring: 5.3.2.1 for the first four places and 3 points for the relay.
220 yards (Seniors, second race): 1 Clarke (M.P.); 2 Whitehorn (W.M.T.); 3 Hayes (B.); 4 Harrison (B.).

Fairclough heads the Juniors---Bicourt the Youths------Hayes the Boys. This is the position at the present time, but who knows how long it will last when we have so many other youngsters striving to depose them?
Fastest times of day:- Bedford (Shaftes) 11.03, Banning (Andover) 11.05, Standing (Brighton) 11.23 Hayes (Wim.Coll) 11.31, Darrant (Shaftes) 11.35, Hough (Hill'n) 11.41

Bill Curtin scored an excellent win in beating Martin of Walton in exactly the same time as last year's winner (Hayes of Mitcham). Showing great form, he improved by 40 seconds on his sixth place of last year and led our team to a useful third place - the same as 12 months ago.
Clos de Hayes 89. -A good year following a poor growth. Frequently up and down but should eventually reward those who can wait.
